accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Technique)
a. Mycoremediation
b. Rhizofiltration
c. Biosparging
d. Rhizoremediation

List-II (Typical application)
i. Absorption or precipitation of contaminants from water by plant roots
ii. Injection of air under pressure below the water table
 iii. Use of fungi for treating organic pollutants
iv. Stimulation of microbes in the rhizosphere by plant roots

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Mycoremediation uses fungi, rhizofiltration uses plant roots to remove contaminants from water, biosparging injects air below the water table, and rhizoremediation involves root–microbe interactions in the rhizosphere.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing an incorrect technique–application match.
accepted.sec: Technique → pollutant or medium treated  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding bioaugmentation and biostimulation:
1. Bioaugmentation introduces specific pollutant-degrading microbes into a contaminated site.
2. Biostimulation enhances the activity of existing microbes by supplying nutrients and oxygen.
3. Oilzapper is an example associated with bioaugmentation, whereas addition of nitrogen and phosphorus to polluted lakes is associated with biostimulation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Bioaugmentation adds pollutant-degrading microbial consortia, while biostimulation supports native microbes through nutrient and oxygen addition.
accepted.tq: Use the meaning–example distinction to separate bioaugmentation from biostimulation.
accepted.sec: Technique → pollutant or medium treated  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Technique — Typical target
o: Biosparging — Contaminated soil through nutrient-supplying wells
Bioventing — Groundwater below the water table
Biostimulation — Polluted water bodies and soil
Rhizofiltration — Volatilisation of contaminants into the atmosphere
accepted.x: Biostimulation is used in polluted water bodies and soil by adding nutrients and oxygen. Bioventing supplies nutrients through wells to contaminated soil, whereas biosparging injects air below the water table.
accepted.tq: Check whether the medium named in each option matches the defining operation of the technique.
accepted.sec: Technique → pollutant or medium treated  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S, consider the following statements:
1. They are bacterial consortia developed by TERI.
2. Their development involved collaboration with Indian Oil.
3. They are used for degrading oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites.
4. They leave no harmful residue after degradation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S are bacterial consortia developed by TERI with Indian Oil. They degrade oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites without leaving harmful residue.
accepted.tq: Test the complete profile of a named technology rather than relying only on its headline application.
accepted.sec: Oil-spill microbes - Oilzapper developer, genetically engineered oil-degrading bacterium  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Oilzapper has also been used at which of the following places?
accepted.x: Oilzapper has been used at Chennai Port for remediation of oil-contaminated material.
accepted.tq: Use the location-specific application as the distinguishing clue.
accepted.sec: Oil-spill microbes - Oilzapper developer, genetically engineered oil-degrading bacterium  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The first genetically engineered oil-eating bacterium, popularly described as a ‘superbug’, was based on:
o: Bacillus subtilis engineered by Norman Borlaug
Escherichia coli engineered by Ian Wilmut
Pseudomonas putida engineered by Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty
Rhizobium leguminosarum engineered by Hargobind Khorana
accepted.x: The first genetically engineered oil-eating bacterium was Pseudomonas putida engineered by Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty.
accepted.tq: Match the organism with the scientist responsible for its engineering.
accepted.sec: Oil-spill microbes - Oilzapper developer, genetically engineered oil-degrading bacterium  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The legal significance associated with Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty’s genetically engineered bacterium is that it was involved in:
o: The first patent for a human gene, affirmed by the International Court of Justice in 1990
The first patent granted for a living organism, affirmed in Diamond v. Chakrabarty in 1980
The first international treaty on genetically modified crops, adopted in 1980
The first patent for a cloned mammal, granted in 1980 by the World Health Organization
accepted.x: The case Diamond v. Chakrabarty, decided by the US Supreme Court in 1980, is associated with the first patenting of a living organism.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal event by linking the case name, year and subject matter.
accepted.sec: Oil-spill microbes - Oilzapper developer, genetically engineered oil-degrading bacterium  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage of bioremediation?
o: It is usually cheaper than conventional clean-up methods
It invariably produces rapid results irrespective of pollutant and site conditions
In-situ treatment can cause little disruption at the contaminated site
It generally uses fewer chemicals and may avoid secondary pollution
accepted.x: Bioremediation is often slow, and its results vary with the pollutant, organism, site conditions and co-contaminants. The other three are recognised advantages.
accepted.tq: Identify the absolute claim that conflicts with the variable performance of biological treatment.
accepted.sec: Advantages and limitations of bioremediation  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the limitations of bioremediation:
1. Its effectiveness may vary with the pollutant, organism and site conditions.
2. Metals and other inorganic contaminants can complicate treatment.
3. Ex-situ methods may require excavation and additional space.
4. Regulation and monitoring may be unnecessary once microbes are introduced.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Bioremediation may require regulation and monitoring; introducing microbes does not make oversight unnecessary.
accepted.tq: Find the single overgeneralised statement among otherwise precise limitations.
accepted.sec: Advantages and limitations of bioremediation  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match the phytoremediation sub-type with its principal process:

List-I (Sub-type)
a. Phytoextraction
b. Phytostabilisation
c. Phytodegradation
d. Phytovolatilisation

List-II (Process)
i. Plant enzymes break down organic pollutants
ii. Contaminants are taken up and released into the air in volatile form
iii. Contaminants are stored in roots and shoots and the plant is harvested
iv. Roots immobilise contaminants and reduce leaching and erosion

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Phytoextraction involves uptake and harvesting, phytostabilisation immobilises contaminants, phytodegradation uses plant enzymes, and phytovolatilisation releases contaminants in volatile form.
accepted.tq: Break each technical term into its process meaning and then verify the full code.
accepted.sec: Phytoremediation sub-types  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Phytovolatilisation — Uptake and release of mercury or selenium in volatile form
Phytostabilisation — Plant enzymes degrade organic contaminants
Phytodegradation — Roots immobilise metals in mine spoils
Phytoextraction — Injection of air below the water table
accepted.x: Phytovolatilisation involves plant uptake followed by release into the air in volatile form; mercury and selenium are examples associated with this process.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the phytoremediation sub-types by the fate of the contaminant after plant uptake.
accepted.sec: Phytoremediation sub-types  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding natural phytoremediators is correct?
o: Eucalyptus removes surplus wastewater mainly by injecting oxygen into groundwater.
Mangroves are used exclusively for thermal treatment of contaminated soil.
Mangroves, estuarine vegetation and wetland vegetation can act as natural phytoremediators, while Eucalyptus along sewage ponds transpires surplus wastewater.
Only desert shrubs can act as natural phytoremediators because wetland plants cannot absorb contaminants.
accepted.x: Mangroves, estuarine vegetation and wetland vegetation are natural phytoremediators. Eucalyptus planted along sewage ponds can transpire surplus wastewater.
accepted.tq: Combine the habitat clue with the plant process instead of confusing phytoremediation with air injection or thermal treatment.
accepted.sec: Phytoremediation sub-types  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match the plant with the principal metal or contaminant associated with its hyperaccumulation:

List-I (Plant)
a. Pteris vittata
b. Brassica juncea
c. Thlaspi (Noccaea) caerulescens
d. Alyssum species

List-II (Metal)
i. Nickel
ii. Arsenic
iii. Zinc and cadmium
iv. Lead, cadmium and selenium

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Pteris vittata accumulates arsenic; Brassica juncea accumulates lead, cadmium and selenium; Thlaspi caerulescens accumulates zinc and cadmium; and Alyssum species accumulate nickel.
accepted.tq: Begin with the distinctive arsenic–fern pair and use elimination for the remaining metals.
accepted.sec: Hyperaccumulator plants → metal accumulated  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about plants used in phytoremediation:
1. Sunflower can accumulate heavy metals, uranium and other radionuclides.
2. Water hyacinth can take up heavy metals and toxic materials from water.
3. Indian mustard is associated with the accumulation of lead, cadmium and selenium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Sunflower, water hyacinth and Indian mustard are associated with the listed contaminant-accumulation roles.
accepted.tq: Check each plant–contaminant association independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Hyperaccumulator plants → metal accumulated  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only biological clean-up methods?
o: Microbial degradation, composting organic waste and constructed wetlands
Thermal treatment, phytoremediation and chemical treatment
Chemical dust suppression, desalination and burning contaminated soil
accepted.x: Microbial degradation, composting and constructed wetlands are biological methods. Incineration, burning, chemical treatment, desalination and excavation are non-biological methods.
accepted.tq: Classify every item by method type before choosing the all-biological set.
accepted.sec: Bioremediation vs non-biological clean-up methods (thermal, chemical)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?

Method — Classification
o: Chemical dust suppressants such as calcium chloride — Chemical
accepted.x: Calcium chloride and magnesium chloride used as chemical dust suppressants represent chemical treatment. Burning is thermal, while desalination and excavation with landfilling are physical methods.
accepted.tq: Use the method of operation to reject the swapped biological, thermal, chemical and physical classifications.
accepted.sec: Bioremediation vs non-biological clean-up methods (thermal, chemical)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A municipal authority uses bacteria to break down organic waste. This activity is best classified as:
accepted.x: The biological breakdown of organic waste by bacteria is microbial degradation and therefore constitutes bioremediation.
accepted.tq: Identify the biological agent and process before distinguishing it from physical or thermal treatment.
accepted.sec: Bioremediation vs non-biological clean-up methods (thermal, chemical)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match the Indian institution with the associated bioremediation product or role:

List-I (Institution)
a. TERI
b. CSIR-NEERI, Nagpur
c. CPCB
d. DBT-BIRAC

List-II (Product or role)
i. Funding biotechnology start-ups developing microbial kits for sewage plants and landfills
ii. Bioremediation of oil-contaminated soils
iii. Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S
aiv. Nodal bioremediation research and development, including heavy-metal removal from effluents

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: TERI is associated with Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S; CSIR-NEERI undertakes nodal bioremediation R&D; CPCB is associated with oil-contaminated soils; and DBT-BIRAC funds relevant biotechnology start-ups.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive TERI–Oilzapper pair and then match the institutional roles.
accepted.sec: Indian research bodies → bioremediation products  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A contaminated lake contains native microbes capable of degradation, but their activity is limited by nutrient deficiency. Which intervention is most appropriate?
o: Add nitrogen and phosphorus to stimulate the native microbes
Harvest plant shoots without addressing microbial activity
Burn the contaminated soil surrounding the lake
Inject air below the water table without adding nutrients
accepted.x: Biostimulation adds nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus, and may also supply oxygen, to enhance the activity of existing microbes in polluted water bodies.
accepted.tq: Ask whether the intervention adds new microbes or improves the performance of microbes already present.
accepted.sec: Technique → pollutant or medium treated  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes rhizofiltration?
o: Fungi degrade organic pollutants in soil
Plant roots absorb or precipitate contaminants from water
Air is injected under pressure below the water table
Plant enzymes convert all metals into volatile gases
accepted.x: Rhizofiltration uses plant roots to absorb or precipitate contaminants from water, particularly metals and radionuclides.
accepted.tq: Use the root-based prefix to distinguish filtration by roots from microbial, air-injection and enzyme-based processes.
accepted.sec: Technique → pollutant or medium treated  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes rhizoremediation?
o: Contaminated soil is excavated and sent to a landfill
Plant roots stimulate microbes in the rhizosphere to address organic pollutants or nutrient imbalance in soil
Contaminants are released into the atmosphere in volatile form by air injection
Plant shoots are harvested after storing contaminants in their tissues
accepted.x: Rhizoremediation depends on plant roots stimulating microbial activity in the rhizosphere and is associated with organic pollutants and nutrient imbalance in soil.
accepted.tq: Distinguish root-zone microbial stimulation from plant harvesting, volatilisation and physical disposal.
accepted.sec: Technique → pollutant or medium treated  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
